In mathematics, especially in [[category theory]], the '''codensity monad''' is a fundamental construction associating a [[monad (category theory)|monad]] to a wide class of [[functor]]s.

==Definition==

The codensity monad of a functor <math>G: D \to C</math> is defined to be the [[Kan extension|right Kan extension]] of <math>G</math> along itself, provided that this Kan extension exists. Thus, by definition it is in particular a functor
<math display=block>T^G : C \to C.</math>
The monad structure on <math>T^G</math> stems from the [[universal property]] of the right Kan extension.

The codensity monad exists whenever <math>D</math> is a small category (has only a set, as opposed to a [[proper class]], of morphisms) and <math>C</math> possesses all (small, i.e., set-indexed) [[limit (category theory)|limit]]s. It also exists whenever <math>G</math> has a [[left adjoint]].

By the general formula computing right Kan extensions in terms of [[end (category theory)|ends]], the codensity monad is given by the following formula:
<math display=block>T^G(c) = \int_{d \in D} G(d)^{C(c, G(d))},</math>
where <math>C(c, G(d))</math> denotes the set of [[morphism]]s in <math>C</math> between the indicated objects and the integral denotes the end. The codensity monad therefore amounts to considering maps from <math>c</math> to an object in the image of <math>G,</math> and maps from the set of such morphisms to <math>G(d),</math> compatible for all the possible <math>d.</math> Thus, as is noted by Avery,{{r|Avery2016}} codensity monads share some kinship with the concept of [[integration (mathematics)|integration]] and double dualization.

==Examples==

===Codensity monads of right adjoints===

If the functor <math>G</math> admits a left adjoint <math>F,</math> the codensity monad is given by the composite <math>G \circ F,</math> together with the standard unit and multiplication maps.

===Concrete examples for functors not admitting a left adjoint===

In several interesting cases, the functor <math>G</math> is an inclusion of a [[full subcategory]] not admitting a left adjoint. For example, the codensity monad of the inclusion of '''[[FinSet]]''' into '''[[Category of sets|Set]]''' is the [[ultrafilter monad]] associating to any set <math>M</math> the set of [[Ultrafilter (set theory)|ultrafilter]]s on <math>M.</math> This was proven by Kennison and Gildenhuys,{{r|KennisonGildenhuys1971}} though without using the term "codensity". In this formulation, the statement is reviewed by [[Tom Leinster|Leinster]].{{sfn|Leinster|2013|loc=§3}}

A related example is discussed by Leinster:{{sfn|Leinster|2013|loc=§7}} the codensity monad of the inclusion of [[finite-dimensional]] [[vector space]]s (over a fixed [[field (mathematics)|field]] <math>k</math>) into all vector spaces is the [[double dualization monad]] given by sending a vector space <math>V</math> to its [[double dual]]
<math display=block>V^{**} = \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Hom}(V, k), k).</math>

Thus, in this example, the end formula mentioned above simplifies to considering (in the notation above) only one object <math>d,</math> namely a one-dimensional vector space, as opposed to considering all objects in <math>D.</math> Adámek and Sousa{{r|AdámekSousa2019}} show that, in a number of situations, the codensity monad of the inclusion
<math display=block>D := C^{fp} \subseteq C</math>
of finitely presented objects (also known as [[compact object (mathematics)|compact object]]s) is a double dualization monad with respect to a sufficiently nice [[injective cogenerator|cogenerating object]]. This recovers both the inclusion of finite sets in sets (where a cogenerator is the set of two elements), and also the inclusion of finite-dimensional vector spaces in vector spaces (where the cogenerator is the ground field).

Sipoş showed that the [[Algebra over a monad|algebras]] over the codensity monad of the inclusion of finite sets (regarded as [[discrete topological space]]s) into topological spaces are equivalent to [[Stone space]]s.{{r|Sipoş2018}}
Avery shows that the [[Giry monad]] arises as the codensity monad of natural [[forgetful functor]]s between certain categories of [[convex space|convex vector space]]s to [[measurable space]]s.{{r|Avery2016}}

==Relation to Isbell duality==

Di Liberti{{sfn|Di Liberti|2019}} shows that the codensity monad is closely related to [[Isbell duality]]: for a given small category <math>C,</math> Isbell duality refers to the adjunction
<math display=block>\mathcal O : Set^{C^{op}} \rightleftarrows (Set^C)^{op} : Spec</math>
between the category of [[presheaf|presheaves]] on <math>C</math> (that is, functors from the opposite category of <math>C</math> to sets) and the opposite category of copresheaves on <math>C.</math> The monad 
<math display=block>Spec \circ \mathcal O</math>
induced by this adjunction is shown to be the codensity monad of the [[Yoneda embedding]] 
<math display=block>y: C \to Set^{C^{op}}.</math>
Conversely, the codensity monad of a full small dense subcategory <math>K</math> in a [[cocomplete category]] <math>C</math> is shown to be induced by Isbell duality.{{sfn|Di Liberti|2019|loc=§2}}
